method: For each gene, fetched RNA tissue/single-cell/blood specificity class and top-3 single-cell expressers (consensus normal-tissue data).
purpose: Compare whether PLAUR/uPAR is more senescence/cell-type-specific than competing senescence surface markers at baseline in normal tissue.
interpretation: At baseline in normal tissue, NONE of the candidate senescence surface markers (PLAUR, GPNMB, DPP4, B2M, TM4SF1, SERPINE1, TSPAN8, NCAM1) is classified 'Cell type specific'; all are 'Cell type enhanced'. The lone truly specific gene tested (MLANA, melanocyte) is shown as a contrast. PLAUR has the single highest immune-cell (myeloid) baseline expression of the panel. Therefore senolytic specificity for any of these antigens cannot derive from absence on normal cells; it must derive from senescence-driven upregulation ABOVE a non-trivial baseline. For uPAR that baseline is especially high on neutrophils/monocytes, constraining the therapeutic window.
limitation: HPA consensus data reflect bulk/normal-tissue baseline expression, not matched senescent-vs-nonsenescent comparisons within a cell type; they bound baseline breadth but do not quantify the senescence-induced fold-change. HPA specificity classes are thresholded categorical calls.
